record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: A complete + pv graph is a graph that can be transformed into a complete graph by deleting at most p vertices. In List Coloring, each vertex has a list of admissible colors and the task is to find a proper coloring that respects all lists. In Precoloring Extension, a partial k-coloring is given and the task is to decide whether it extends to a proper k-coloring of the whole graph. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of List Coloring and of Precoloring Extension on complete + pv graphs?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Determine the complexity of List Coloring and Precoloring Extension for complete+pv graphs when parameterized by p.

F + pe, F - pe, F + pv and F - pv, which consist of all graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by deleting at most p edges, adding at most p edges, deleting at most p vertices and adding at most p vertices, respectively.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a nonnegative integer $p$, call a graph $G$ a "complete $+pv$" graph if there exists a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|\le p$ such that $G-S$ is a complete graph. Consider the following two problems on complete $+pv$ graphs:

(1) List Coloring: each vertex $v$ is given a list $L(v)$ of admissible colors; decide whether there is a proper coloring $c$ of $G$ with $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every vertex $v$.

(2) Precoloring Extension: given an integer $k$ and a partial proper $k$-coloring of a subset of vertices of $G$, decide whether it extends to a proper $k$-coloring of all of $G$.

Determine the parameterized complexity of List Coloring and of Precoloring Extension on complete $+pv$ graphs when parameterized by $p$. In particular, decide for each problem whether it is fixed-parameter tractable, admits a polynomial kernel, or is $\mathrm{W}[1]$-hard with respect to $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved by Hermelin, Kratsch, and others (STACS 2020): with respect to the size $k$ of a clique modulator (equivalently the parameter $p$ for complete $+pv$ graphs), List Coloring admits an $O^*(2^k)$ randomized FPT algorithm, and Precoloring Extension admits a kernel with at most $3k$ vertices. This directly answers the open question.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Pre-Coloring Extension and List Coloring Problems
status_evidence.snippet: For List Coloring with a clique modulator D of size k, an O*(2^k)-time randomized algorithm; for Pre-Coloring Extension a kernel with at most 3k vertices, addressing open questions of Golovach, Paulusma, and Song.
status_evidence.claim: Both problems are FPT parameterized by the clique modulator size p, with Precoloring Extension admitting a linear-vertex kernel.
